newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST-Russian GDP likely to grow in June yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Russian GDP likely to grow in June yr/yr.

text.p: Russia's gross domestic product is likely to grow in June on a year-on-year basis, as output last June was low, a senior State Statistics Committee official said on Monday.

"Our year's final GDP result will depend on June-July figures," Deputy Chairman Vladimir Sokolin told a news conference. "I would not be surprised if these months give us a rise as last June the whole country stopped working."
In the first five months of 1997 Russia's GDP was 0.2 percent lower than a year earlier.
"From a macroeconomic point of view we are in a period of stabilisation," Sokolin said.
He said trade and industry were registering growth of one and 0.2 percent respectively, and 1997 was the first year when investment in industry had not fallen.
Output in the construction sector fell eight percent in the first five months of 1997 after a 20 percent fall in the same period last year, he said.
